Class StatisticsKernel

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.dod.StatisticsKernel
public class StatisticsKernel extends Object

Statistics Kernel

Computes first-order macroeconomic and demographic aggregates (Lorenz/Milanovic Gini, physical-capital Gross World Product, Gompertz-Makeham life expectancy, and Total Fertility Rate) directly from conserved cellular and cohort observables (AGENTS.md §10.1, §10.4), with zero dependency on synthetic technologyLevel scalars.

Version:
1.0.0-beta.3
Author:
Silvere Martin-Michiellot

    float
    calculateGini(float[] values)
    Computes the exact Lorenz Gini inequality coefficient for a given resource or wealth array: $$G = \frac{2 \sum_{i=1}^{n} i \cdot x_i}{n \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i} - \frac{n + 1}{n}$$
    float
    calculateGini(float[] capital, float[] humanBiomass)
    Computes the societal wealth/resource Gini coefficient across inhabited cells directly from physical capital per capita ($K_i / N_i$), constrained by the Milanovic, Lindert & Williamson (2011) Inequality Possibility Frontier (IPF): $$G_{\text{IPF}}(\alpha) = \frac{\alpha - 1}{\alpha}, \quad \alpha = \frac{\bar{k}}{k_{\text{sub}}}$$
    float

    Computes life expectancy from cohort mean ages and full nutritional satisfaction when no WorldBuffer is provided (Lotka stable age distribution $e_0 \approx 1.35 \bar{a}$).

      public float calculateGini(float[] values)
      Computes the exact Lorenz Gini inequality coefficient for a given resource or wealth array: $$G = \frac{2 \sum_{i=1}^{n} i \cdot x_i}{n \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i} - \frac{n + 1}{n}$$

    • calculateGini

      public float calculateGini(float[] capital, float[] humanBiomass)
      Computes the societal wealth/resource Gini coefficient across inhabited cells directly from physical capital per capita ($K_i / N_i$), constrained by the Milanovic, Lindert & Williamson (2011) Inequality Possibility Frontier (IPF): $$G_{\text{IPF}}(\alpha) = \frac{\alpha - 1}{\alpha}, \quad \alpha = \frac{\bar{k}}{k_{\text{sub}}}$$
      Parameters:
      capital - array of cellular physical capital stocks ($K_i$)
      humanBiomass - array of cellular agent populations ($N_i$)
      Returns:
      societal Gini coefficient bounded in $[0.15, 0.78]$

    • calculateGDP

      public float calculateGDP(float[] capital, float[] humanBiomass, double totalWatts)
      Calculates Gross World Product (GWP) annual flow in 1990 Geary-Khamis USD directly from conserved physical capital stock ($Y = K / \beta$, Piketty 2014 $\beta \approx 3.5$) and metabolic subsistence baseline ($400\,\text{GK\$}/\text{capita}$, Maddison 2020), blended smoothly ($C^\infty$). /** Evaluates Gross World Product (GWP) using the Ayres & Warr (2009) / Kümmel (2011) physical Exergy-Augmented Cobb-Douglas production function anchored to the Maddison Project (2020) physiological subsistence baseline ($Y_0 = 102\text{ Int\$1990/capita}$): $$Y = N \cdot Y_0 \cdot \left(\frac{\max(P_{\text{somatic}}, p)}{P_{\text{somatic}}}\right)^{\alpha_E} \cdot \left(1 + \frac{k_{\text{pc}}}{k_0}\right)^{\alpha_K}$$ with empirical output elasticities $\alpha_E = 0.65$ (useful power exergy) and $\alpha_K = 0.35$ (built capital stock), somatic hearth baseline $P_{\text{somatic}} = 348\text{ W/capita}$, and traditional village capital scale $k_0 = 120\text{ kg/capita}$.
      Parameters:
      capital - array of cellular physical capital stocks ($K_i$ in kg)
      totalWatts - aggregate useful mechanical/thermal/electrical power dissipation ($\text{W}$)
      humanPopulation - array of cellular agent populations ($N_i$ headcount)
      Returns:
      annual GWP flow in 1990 Geary-Khamis USD

    • calculateLifeExpectancy

      public float calculateLifeExpectancy(WorldBuffer world, float foodSatisfaction)
      Computes population-weighted life expectancy at birth directly from cellular lifespan, physical sanitary capital per capita ($K/N$), potable water availability, and nutritional satisfaction (Preston 1975 curve + Omran 1971 epidemiological transition, zero technology scalar).
      Parameters:
      world - world buffer containing physical observables
      foodSatisfaction - aggregate nutritional satisfaction ratio in $[0, 1]$
      Returns:
      life expectancy at birth in years, bounded in $[15.0, 86.0]$
